source.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Shi-Yuan Feng; Huan Gao; Haohan Chi; Han Wu; Zhi-Long Zhang; Zheng Jiang; Bing-Xiang He; Wei-Ying Ma; Ya-Qin Zhang; Hao Zhou

page_placements.theme: Training dynamics: early student gains, then regression as the student fits supervisor errors or over-optimises the teacher's signal
Transferring a weaker model's training shift (RL policy shift, update vectors, contrast against a weaker predictor) to a stronger model

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a signal derived from weaker-model RL can improve stronger students, but transfers a post-RL/reference policy shift rather than fine-tuning on weak-model labels and does not calculate PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Direct-OPD transfer outcomes, comparisons with vanilla OPD and direct RL, and analyses of top-k overlap, response length, and KL settings. It does not report PGR or a true-label-trained strong-model ceiling. Entropy diagnostics are not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure task performance or the named versions.
record.test_reason: A different training method aimed at the same question: a weaker supervisor (JustRL-1.5B, 51.3/37.5 on AIME24/25) trains stronger or comparable students. The supervision is the weak model's RL-induced log-ratio used as an implicit reward, not weak labels. The paper reports student accuracy against the weak teacher and compares with naive on-policy imitation of that teacher. It computes no PGR and reports no converged strong ceiling. Only the JustRL pair is weak-to-strong; the QuestA teacher (72.5/62.29) is stronger than every student it trains.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a small RL teacher's policy shift (post-RL vs pre-RL log-ratio, read as an implicit reward) can be applied on a stronger student's own states to improve it, even when the student already exceeds the teacher. They report that it transfers across teacher pairs and student families, beats step-matched direct RL at lower compute, and composes sequentially. They add that the signal is conditional: it can fail when the shift is not meaningful on student-visited states, and the best response length and KL are pair-dependent.
record.recipe_differences: Instead of fine-tuning on labels produced by a weak model, Direct-OPD uses the token-level log-ratio between a weak model's post-RL checkpoint and its pre-RL reference as a dense signal on student on-policy states, with a KL anchor to the student's initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with teacher-student pair, response length, and KL coefficient. The best fixed KL coefficient differs by pair; the 6k response-length run validates below the 2k run at the stated checkpoint.

fits_no_version.finding: Running RL on a 1.5B model and transferring its shift beats step-matched direct RL on R1-Distill-7B. A Qwen3-1.7B RL shift brings Qwen3-4B-nonthinking to the direct-RL level (0.635).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak-to-strong transfer of RL signals can match or beat compute- or step-matched direct RL on the strong model.

fits_no_version.finding: Accuracy depends on training horizon and KL strength. At 6k horizon the student falls below its initial accuracy (45.6 vs 48.3). A larger implicit reward does not track better validation. The authors attribute this to an unreliable supervisor signal on off-distribution states, without testing it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Implicit-reward weak-to-strong transfer degrades when the student drifts off the weak supervisor's support (possible V4-like exploitation, untested).

fits_no_version.finding: Transfer gains occur without rising teacher–student top-k overlap in cross-pattern settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-level imitation overlap is not necessary for gains from a policy-shift signal.

fits_no_version.finding: Policy shifts from two teacher pairs (QuestA stronger than the student) compose sequentially: 63.8/46.8 after both stages vs 58.3/43.2 after JustRL alone.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independent RL-derived shifts compose in one student.

record.problems: PGR is not calculated and no strong model trained on true labels is reported as a ceiling. The core results are on math benchmarks; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Some analysis values are only plotted, and the paper notes that transfer can fail when the teacher/reference signal is not meaningful on student-visited states.
record.rows_left_out: Entropy diagnostics in Figures 6 and 10 were omitted because they measure entropy rather than task performance or one of the named claim versions. Figure 7's response-length curves were not separately recorded because the comparable explicit step-40 accuracy values are captured in r16; the other curve values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Ordinary fine-tuning on weak labels; PGR; a strong model trained to convergence on ground truth as ceiling. Weak-to-strong in the strict sense (student initially below supervisor) only for Qwen3-1.7B.
Auxiliary confidence loss, supervisor ensembles, and other listed loss variants. Effect on PGR. Only one model and benchmark for the Direct-OPD vs naive-OPD comparison.
PGR as a function of size; tasks beyond competition math (NLP classification, chess, reward modelling); a formal predictor analysis.
Not tested. Off-distribution unreliability of the supervisor signal is hypothesised for long horizons and weak KL but not measured. No shared-error, checkability or external distribution-shift test.
Not tested. The policy-as-reward identity is derived, but no conditions under which the student must beat its supervisor.

missing.what: Transfer quality depends on which weak-teacher RL checkpoint is used: T300 carries a weaker shift than T900–T1500 (figure only). This bears on supervisor quality as a predictor.

Scores of the weak teachers at T300–T1500, and of Qwen3-1.7B-nonthinking RL and the initial Qwen3-4B-nonthinking. These are needed to place the student relative to supervisor and to the direct-RL quasi-ceiling (figure only, if at all).

record.verdict_notes: Strict weak-to-strong evidence is narrow: one weak teacher pair, and only Qwen3-1.7B starts below its supervisor. The QuestA experiments use a teacher stronger than the students and should not count as weak-to-strong. No PGR, ceiling or uncertainty is reported, and the r11 value (~50) is read from a figure. The record's V4 limits_scope label is dropped: the horizon and KL results are hyperparameter sensitivities with an untested explanation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not use weak-model labels for ordinary fine-tuning, report PGR, or give a strong model trained on true labels as a ceiling.
Tests Direct-OPD against vanilla OPD, not the listed auxiliary-confidence, ensemble-supervisor, or other loss variants; does not report PGR.
Tests math benchmarks, several language-model sizes/families, and top-k overlap; not NLP tasks beyond math, chess, reward modelling, or a broad predictor analysis.

The paper discusses unreliable teacher/reference signals on student-visited off-distribution prefixes and tests response-length/KL conditions, but does not test weak-supervisor checkability, shared errors, or an external distribution shift.
Derives an objective identity but does not establish conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

relation.reason: Reports student performance against weak-teacher performance and compares transfer methods.

tranche.reason: Transfers a weak model's RL-induced policy shift on student trajectories, testing the weak-supervision question with a different training method.

source_check.notes: Direct-OPD uses checkpoint log-ratios rather than weak labels; no strong ceiling or PGR is reported. QuestA and composition results use a stronger teacher, and the horizon summary confuses single-benchmark initialization with two-benchmark validation.

statements.correction: Qwen3-1.7B: AIME24 48.3→58.3, teacher 51.3; AIME25 36.8→43.2, teacher 37.5. Comparators: vanilla OPD in Figure 1(a), direct RL in Section 3.2. No PGR or uncertainty estimates reported.
statements.problem: The Direct-OPD scores are correct, but the blanket assertion of no controls overlooks vanilla-OPD and direct-RL comparisons.

statements.correction: Direct-OPD versus vanilla OPD: R1-Distill-7B on AIME24, 63.1 versus roughly 50, initial 56.7. Main transfer experiments: three students across two families, AIME24 and AIME25. Only the vanilla-OPD comparison is restricted to one student and benchmark.
statements.problem: The comparison scores are correct; saying the study has one model and one benchmark understates its scope.

statements.correction: Vanilla-OPD comparison: R1-Distill-7B, AIME24, Direct-OPD 63.1 versus OPD roughly 50. Main transfer experiments: Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, R1-Distill-7B; AIME24 and AIME25.

statements.correction: Figure 8, step 40: 2k 48.8, 4k 48.3, 6k 45.6. Initial AIME24/AIME25: 48.3/36.8; 45.6 exceeds their mean. Larger diagnostic shift need not improve validation. Unreliable late-prefix supervision: proposed explanation.
